thread:
maya: Quick thread 1 — I'm opening a PR to add a tiny onboarding YAML generator and a migration checklist for Dedicated Capacity docs. Aim: reduce copy/paste errors and clarify isolation behavior across regions.

jay: Nice. Can the generator also emit a Terraform snippet? Many teams start from TF.

manika: (typo) it's anika :) Yes please include TF. Could we add a column in the tenant matrix for `multi-region-failover` implied behavior? That's tripped folks before.

maya: Good call. Plan: generator outputs three artefacts: YAML for operators, JS SDK snippet, and Terraform module scaffold. I'll add an appendix that maps fields across the three.

jay: For autoscale examples, add a short burst policy sample. Folks confuse cooldown vs burst windows. Example I like:
```yaml
scalePolicy:
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 40
  cooldown: 180
  burstWindowSeconds: 30
  burstCapacity: 5
```

anika: Love it. Also include a short note about how burst interacts with committed reserved pools vs shared pools. e.g., burst uses spare capacity in the reserved pool if available; otherwise it falls back to transient nodes and may be preempted.

rob: Heads-up: the infra repo renamed the Terraform module from `redwood/dedicated` -> `infra/dedicated-capacity` last week. There's a broken link in the runbook. I'll paste a quick sed patch in the PR comments.

maya: Thanks — I'll update links. Also adding a small migration checklist for teams moving from shared to dedicated: rotate keys, pin model versions, dry-run traffic shift, run smoke tests in region, update alert rules.

jay: Could we add an example CSV-to-YAML mapping for large tenant imports? Real customers sometimes upload CSVs. A one-liner Python snippet to convert would be helpful.

anika: I'll draft that Python snippet. Keep it minimal: read CSV, validate labels, emit YAML.

maya: Added a docs/examples/dedicated/csv-to-yaml.py example and referenced it. Also added a short paragraph explaining "isolation modes": committed (reserved, no preemption), burst-committed (reserved plus temporary burst allowed), and best-effort (shared, preemptible).

rob: Tiny wording nit: the SLA section currently says "Committed: p95 200ms" which reads like a guarantee. Suggest change to "Illustrative p95 target: ~200ms under provisioned load" and add a link to the SLA legal page for enterprise.

anika: Agreed. Also suggest a short FAQ entry: "What happens during regional failover?" with steps and an example sequence (promote standby region -> update routing -> warm caches).

maya: Added FAQ and an example failover runbook snippet. Also included a caution: "If cross-region failover is required, contact SRE for capacity booking; auto-failover may incur additional charges."

docs-bot: PR opened by maya: PR #998 — "Dedicated onboarding generator + migration checklist + examples". Requested reviewers: jay, anika. Preview build queued: https://preview.docs.redwood.ai/pr-998

jay: Left two inline comments: one asks to convert the YAML example to use camelCase keys matching SDK samples, another asks for a one-line summary at the top of the runbook.

maya: Updated branch: switched keys to camelCase in examples and added a one-paragraph TL;DR. Pushed.

rob: Pushed a tiny patch that fixes the Terraform module link and updates the module source block example.

anika: Drafted the CSV converter and added validation note about reserved label values (e.g., `reserved_pool`, `no_preempt`).

maya: Great. Merging once CI green + two approvals. If anyone spots text that could be misread as a contractual SLA, flag here.

jay: :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks team — this should cut a lot of onboarding friction.
